content: Twinfilin-1 is a protein in humans that is encoded by the TWF1 gene. This gene produces twinfilin, a protein that binds to actin monomers and is evolutionarily conserved across species ranging from yeast to mammals. Research on the mouse homolog of this protein indicates that twinfilin-1 may function as an actin monomer-binding protein. Its localization to cortical structures rich in G-actin appears to be regulated by the small GTPase RAC1. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of TWF1. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Twf1tm1a(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This initiative is a large-scale mutagenesis project aimed at generating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers. Male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of the gene deletion. A total of 23 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, but no significant abnormalities were detected.
